html:
A Native American religious movement that spread across the American West in 1889 and 1890. It was crushed at the Wounded Knee Massacre.

It began with Wovoka, a Northern Paiute prophet in Nevada, who had a vision during a solar eclipse on 1 January 1889. He taught that if people danced a round dance, lived honestly and kept peace with whites, the dead would return, the game would come back and the old world would be renewed.

By then the bison were gone and the peoples of the Plains were confined to reservations, often hungry. The teaching spread quickly from nation to nation. Among the Lakota, some believers wore "ghost shirts" they thought would stop bullets.

US officials saw the dances as a threat. In December 1890 police killed Sitting Bull while trying to arrest him. Two weeks later, at Wounded Knee in South Dakota, US soldiers killed around 250 to 300 Lakota, many of them women and children. The massacre is often seen as the end of the Indian Wars.
sum: A Native American religious movement that spread across the American West in 1889 and 1890. It was crushed at the Wounded Knee Massacre.
